problems.title: An unconditional fallback can defeat goal validation
problems.source_location: Section 4.3, Eq.(8), p.5; Appendix A.2, Algorithm 2; Appendix A.3, Figure 8; lazySI.py, forward, lines 1111–1154
claim: When the proposed skill fails goal validation, the printed rule ranks state proximity over \(A(g)\cup\{z_h\}\), where \(A(g)\) contains goal-valid skills. The following prose says the rejected proposal \(z_h\) is only a fallback when no valid candidate exists.
analysis: Take two skills, proposal \(z_h=1\), state \(s=0\), and goal \(g=10\). Give the state prototypes means \(0,1\), the goal prototypes means \(0,10\), and every Gaussian variance \(1\). With threshold \(\sqrt{\chi^2_{1,0.99}}\approx2.575829\), skill \(1\) fails goal validation and skill \(2\) passes. The unconditional union nevertheless ranks skill \(1\) first because its state distance is \(0\), versus \(1\). Four duplicate prototypes satisfy the stated prototype count; small perturbations preserve the strict inequalities. The same construction embeds in \(60\) dimensions with identity covariance, whose threshold is approximately \(9.401<10\). In contrast, the author implementation collects valid candidates and introduces its nearest-goal fallback only when that collection is empty, so it avoids this example.
result: The current printed candidate formula does not enforce its own stated fallback semantics. This is a paper/implementation specification inconsistency, with no demonstrated current-code failure or reward reduction.
repair: Make the rule conditional: retain \(z_h\) if it is valid; otherwise rank over \(A(g)\) when nonempty; use an explicitly chosen fallback only when \(A(g)=\varnothing\). Align the empty-set fallback with the implementation, which uses nearest goal proximity rather than necessarily returning \(z_h\).
problems.existing_correction_status: The official supplemental implementation and current public implementation already avoid the demonstrated failure. The latest paper formula still contains the unconditional union.
problems.impact_rationale: The defect is a bounded decision-rule specification error; the released implementation already excludes the invalid proposal in this case.
